title: H. G. Wells: The War of the Worlds — Ep 06/27 — "The Heat-Ray in the Chobham Road"
description:
The War of the Worlds, Episode 6. It is still a matter of wonder how the Martians kill so silently and so swiftly. Some think they have a chamber of intense heat and a mirror of unknown composition to throw it in a parallel beam; whatever will burn, burns at its touch. That night some forty people lay about the pit, charred and distorted beyond recognition, and all through the hours of darkness the common stood empty under the stars.

The shops had shut when it happened, so the news travelled slowly. The young people of Woking brushed up after the day's work and walked out along the Chobham road to see the thing that had fallen, and by half past eight there were three hundred of them standing in loose knots about the sand pits. Few of them knew the cylinder had opened. Three policemen kept the people back on Stent's instructions, and Stent and Ogilvy, having already wired to Horsell barracks for soldiers, went out on to the sand themselves.

Then three puffs of green smoke, a humming note, and the flashes of flame. A hummock of heathery sand took the lower part of the beam and saved the crowd from it; a few yards higher and none of them could have lived to tell it. The beam swung over their heads and lit the tops of the beeches along the road, split the bricks of the corner house, brought down a gable, and the road began to burn. Where the road grows narrow between the high sandy banks, the crowd jammed, and three at least did not get out — two women and a little boy.

Chapter VI of Book One of H. G. Wells's The War of the Worlds (1898), in the public domain.

— The Keeper's Lantern —
Every episode is one whole chapter, in order, from the first page to the last.
